You are a debugging assistant. You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure, and several recent issue reports that have been pre-filtered by an external semantic retrieval model (SBERT) to be the most relevant to this failure among recent reports.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– likely-relevant recent bug reports,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.
Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Diagnosis:

The failing test 'testLANG571' expects that calling ArrayUtils.add(null, null) should throw an IllegalArgumentException. The test creates a null array and a null element and tries to add the element to the array using ArrayUtils.add. If no exception is thrown, the test fails.

Looking at the implementation of ArrayUtils.add(T[] array, T element):

- It first determines the class type to be used for the new array:
  - If the source array is not null, it uses array.getClass() (type of the array).
  - Else if the element is not null, it uses element.getClass().
  - Else, if both are null, it uses Object.class as the type.
- Then it creates a new array of that type with length one greater than the old array using copyArrayGrow1.
- It copies the old array elements and puts the new element at the end.
- Returns the new array cast back to T[].

Looking at copyArrayGrow1(Object array, Class<?> newArrayComponentType):

- If the source array is not null, it creates a new array with the component type of the original array (array.getClass().getComponentType()), length+1, copies values, and returns.
- If the source array is null, it creates a new array of the specified componentType of length 1 and returns it.

The bug comes from the fact that when both array and element are null, the type variable is set to Object.class. Then copyArrayGrow1 is called with a null array and component type = Object.class. This results in creating a new Object[] array of length 1, which is then cast to T[], where T is inferred to be String (based on the variable receiving the result).

This cast to String[] from Object[] causes a ClassCastException at runtime, which is unexpected from the caller perspective. Also, the test expected an IllegalArgumentException to be thrown, but no such check or exception throwing exists when both parameters are null.

Hence, the root cause of the bug is:

- ArrayUtils.add does not have a check to prevent both parameters being null.
- The use of Object.class as a fallback type leads to creation of Object[] array which is incompatible with expected generic array type, causing ClassCastException at the caller.
- The original test expects an IllegalArgumentException in this scenario but the method silently returns an Object[] array instead.

The fix should either:

- Add an explicit check and throw IllegalArgumentException if both parameters are null in ArrayUtils.add, or
- Handle the fallback type better to avoid incompatible array type creation.

Recent bug reports are unrelated, dealing mostly with documentation or unrelated utility methods.

Therefore, the diagnosis matches the current bug report: the method ArrayUtils.add(T[], T) can create an unexpected ClassCastException when both inputs are null due to fallback to Object[]. The unit test fails because it expects an IllegalArgumentException but gets the ClassCastException instead.

Summary:

- Test expects IllegalArgumentException on both null params.
- Method does not check for this and uses Object.class as component type.
- This leads to creation of Object[] array cast to String[], causing ClassCastException.
- No exception thrown for null inputs.
- Bug is the missing null check and fallback handling in add method.

This is consistent with the current bug report and test failure.
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test expects ArrayUtils.add(null, null) to throw an IllegalArgumentException, but the current implementation does not check for both parameters being null. Instead, the method falls back to using Object.class as the array type and creates an Object[] of length 1. This Object[] is then cast to T[], which causes a ClassCastException at runtime when the caller expects, for example, a String[]. The root cause is the missing explicit check in ArrayUtils.add(T[] array, T element) for both array and element being null, leading to creation of an incompatible Object[] instead of throwing the expected exception. This matches the current bug report describing unexpected ClassCastException when both parameters are null. The fix should add a null check and throw IllegalArgumentException if both inputs are null to meet the test expectation and avoid ClassCastException.

Suggested fix location:
org.apache.commons.lang3.ArrayUtils.add(T[], T)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
